object: LocHal Public Library, Tilburg — exposed hall frame and inserted stair/library levels
creator: CIVIC architects (architecture), Braaksma & Roos (restoration), Inside Outside / Petra Blaisse (interior concept/textiles), Mecanoo (library interior)
work_date: Original locomotive hall 1932, per CIVIC; renovation/interior realization 2018, per Mecanoo
photo_date: not separately established by the inspected provider page
branch: Industrial adaptive-reuse interior in a former locomotive hall
rights: Copyright Stijn Bollaert; no open reuse license established
rights_evidence: CIVIC explicitly assigns photographic image rights to Stijn Bollaert; this exact linked gallery file includes the same credit. No CC/PD permission is stated.
attribution: Stijn Bollaert, LocHal Public Library Tilburg, published by CIVIC architects in its project gallery. Public architectural preview; no general reuse license established.
claim_scope: A contemporary industrial adaptive-reuse interior whose exposed hall frame, roof construction, large window grid and new library circulation are jointly visible. Historic reuse and present formal organization are separate evidence; not every reused factory automatically has an industrial-looking interior.
observable_features: A high exposed roof of repeated trusses, beams and suspended service/lighting tracks spans the open interior.
Large gridded glazing and repeated tall dark vertical members set the hall scale and organize several levels.
New stairs, glass-edged landings, book rows and restrained reading furniture sit within the larger frame rather than covering it with a closed ceiling.
Riveted/paint-varied older-looking frame elements coexist with darker new-looking insertions; two small people at the lower edge do not obscure the roof, bays or stairs.
limits: The people and small wayfinding signs remain real parts of the public interior, but do not dominate the defining frame. The image cannot prove which member bears load, service operation, hidden material composition or structural safety. Exact old/new component assignments and dates come from project documentation, not visual aging alone. Do not infer that darkness, rust, an old factory address or one metal lamp is necessary or sufficient for industrial style.

association_evidence.supports: CIVIC identifies the former 1932 locomotive hall, contemporary reinterpretation of its industrial logic, large open space, exposed basic steel/concrete/glass/wood relationships and named team. The exact photo is linked in the gallery and credited to Stijn Bollaert.

Mecanoo documents the 2018 interior realization, the named design-team roles, former locomotive-hall program, old industrial columns and new oak/steel insertions. Its own photo credit is different and does not license the selected CIVIC/Stijn Bollaert image.
